# v1.1.0-dev.106: Virtual Windows that look the part

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.105`.

## Docked windows leave the taskbar

A docked window's taskbar button now goes away while it's docked. The virtual
window's own button brings it and everything in it forward, so the taskbar shows
one button for the lot. Docked windows stay in alt-tab.

The buttons come back when you undock a window, close or delete its virtual
window, or turn this off in Settings, under Virtual Windows. If WLM stops
unexpectedly, the same watcher that puts fully docked windows back gives the
buttons back too.

## An icon of their own

Virtual windows have their own icon: the WLM panes inside a window frame. It's on
their taskbar button, in alt-tab and on their title bar, and it marks them in the
app. They also share a taskbar group of their own instead of joining WLM's.

## Start fresh, or use the window that's open

The window editor's "start it again" box is now a choice:

- Use the window that's open.
- Use the open window, or start it if none is.
- Always start a new one, even when one is already open.

This works for any app now, not only Explorer folders and consoles. WLM starts it
from the program the window was saved from, and only when that program still
exists and has the app's name. A window started fresh never takes over the one
that was already open.

## The Virtual Windows page, like a profile

The page shows one virtual window at a time, picked from tabs, with the same List
and Visual views a profile has. The virtual window is the monitor.

- List has a row for each docked window, with its pane, how it starts when a
  profile loads, and a button to undock it.
- Visual draws the virtual window and its panes. Drag a window onto another to
  swap them, or onto an edge to put it beside.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
